literal: After several days he fled away; Youzhou commander Zhou Dewei received him.
idiomatic: Within days he slipped away, and Zhou Dewei, commander of Youzhou, took him in.

literal: When an edict came demanding his return, Dewei spoke insolently, and a southern campaign was then debated.
idiomatic: When the court ordered him handed back, Dewei answered with insolence, and the court began to plan a campaign south.

literal: In the tenth month of winter, on day wushen, he went ice fishing on the Yalu River.
idiomatic: That winter, in the tenth month, on wushen day, he went ice fishing on the Yalu River.

literal: Silla sent envoys bearing tribute goods; Goryeo sent envoys presenting a precious sword; the King of Wuyue, Qian, sent Teng Yanxiu with tribute.
idiomatic: Silla sent envoys with regional products; Goryeo sent envoys bearing a treasured sword; and Qian, King of Wuyue, dispatched Teng Yanxiu with tribute.

literal: That year the Junji Taiyi deity appeared repeatedly; an edict ordered his likeness painted.
idiomatic: That year the Junji Taiyi god was seen again and again, and the Emperor ordered his image drawn.

literal: On day bingchen in the third month, Helu, yilijin of the Dieci branch, was made Aluduo li yuyue; the hundred officials were advanced in rank and rewards distributed in varying measure, and a three-day grant was bestowed.
idiomatic: On bingchen day in the third month, Helu, yilijin of the Dieci branch, was appointed Aluduo li yuyue; officials were promoted and gifts handed out in due measure, and the court granted three days' leave.

literal: His son Bei was installed as crown prince.
idiomatic: His son Bei was named crown prince.

literal: On the yiyou new moon in the fourth month of summer, Lu Guoyong, Jin's military governor of Youzhou, came to surrender; <8> he was made Youzhou military and cavalry acting commissioner.
idiomatic: On the yiyou new moon of the fourth summer month, Lu Guoyong, Jin's governor of Youzhou, defected; <8> he was appointed acting military and cavalry commissioner of Youzhou.

literal: On day jiachen, Liang sent Lang Gongyuan to offer congratulations.
idiomatic: On jiachen day Liang dispatched Lang Gongyuan with congratulations.

literal: On day gengyin in the sixth month, the King of Wuyue sent Teng Yanxiu with tribute.
idiomatic: On gengyin day in the sixth month, the King of Wuyue sent Teng Yanxiu with tribute.

literal: On day renshen in the seventh month of autumn, he personally campaigned against the Turks, Tuguhun, Xiang, Lesser Fan, Shatuo, and other tribes, and pacified them all.
idiomatic: On renshen day in the seventh autumn month he took the field in person against the Turks, Tuguhun, Xiang, Lesser Fan, Shatuo, and the rest, and brought them all to heel.

literal: He captured their chieftains together with fifteen thousand six hundred households, more than nine hundred thousand suits of armor, weapons, and gear, and treasure, camels, horses, cattle, and sheep beyond reckoning.
idiomatic: He took their chieftains and fifteen thousand six hundred households captive, along with more than nine hundred thousand pieces of armor, arms, and equipment, and treasure, camels, horses, cattle, and sheep past all count.

literal: In the eighth month, he seized Shuozhou and captured its military governor Li Siben.
idiomatic: In the eighth month he overran Shuozhou and took its governor Li Siben prisoner.

literal: He carved stone to record the achievement south of the Green Mound.
idiomatic: He had his victory cut in stone south of the Green Mound.

literal: On the guiwei new moon in the tenth month of winter, riding the victory he marched east.
idiomatic: That winter, on the guiwei new moon of the tenth month, he pressed east while the momentum held.

literal: In the eleventh month, he attacked the five prefectures of Yu, Xin, Wu, Gui, and Ru, and took more than fourteen thousand seven hundred heads.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month he struck Yu, Xin, Wu, Gui, and Ru—five prefectures in all—and claimed more than fourteen thousand seven hundred heads.

literal: From north of Dai to the Yin Mountains at the river bend, he held all the land.
idiomatic: From north of Dai to the Yin Mountains along the river bend, the whole country fell to him.

literal: He then changed Wu Prefecture to Guihua Prefecture and Gui Prefecture to Khan Prefecture, established the Southwest Pacification Office, and chose men of merit to command it.
idiomatic: He renamed Wu Prefecture Guihua Prefecture and Gui Prefecture Khan Prefecture, set up a Southwest Pacification Office, and put proven men in charge.

literal: When they invested Yu Prefecture, the enemy towers collapsed for no reason; the army raised a great clamor and pressed the chance, and the city fell before long.
idiomatic: At the siege of Yu Prefecture the watchtowers gave way without cause; the troops broke into a roar and rushed the breach, and the city fell in no time.

literal: At that time envoys from both Liang and Wuyue were present; by edict they were led around the city to watch, and Teng Yanxiu was granted the name Qiulü.
idiomatic: Envoys from Liang and Wuyue were there at the time; the Emperor had them led around the walls to witness the fall, and bestowed on Teng Yanxiu the name Qiulü.

literal: In the twelfth month, he recovered the eight armies north of the mountains.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month he retook the eight armies north of the mountains.

literal: In the second month of spring in the second year, Lu Wenjin, Jin's deputy general of Xin Prefecture, killed military governor Li Cunju and came to surrender.
idiomatic: In the second year, in the second spring month, Lu Wenjin, a Jin deputy commander at Xin Prefecture, killed Governor Li Cunju and defected.

literal: Advancing to attack the city, Prefect An Jinquan fled; Wenjin's subordinate general Liu Yin was made prefect.
idiomatic: He marched on the city; Prefect An Jinquan fled, and Wenjin's officer Liu Yin was installed as prefect.

literal: On day xinhai in the third month, he attacked Youzhou; military governor Zhou Dewei, with troops from the five prefectures of You, Bing, Zhen, Ding, and Wei, blocked him west of Juyong Pass; they joined battle east of Xin Prefecture, routed him utterly, took more than thirty thousand heads, and killed Li Si'en's son Wuba.
idiomatic: On xinhai day in the third month he invested Youzhou. Zhou Dewei, governor of Youzhou, barred the way west of Juyong Pass with forces from You, Bing, Zhen, Ding, and Wei; east of Xin Prefecture they met in battle, broke the Khitan host, took more than thirty thousand heads, and killed Wuba, son of Li Si'en.

literal: <9> Thereafter his younger brother Aguqi was made commander-in-chief and Shilu vanguard; they marched east out of the pass to sweep Yan and Zhao, met no enemy, and returned.
idiomatic: <9> Then his brother Aguqi was made supreme commander and Shilu led the van; they went east through the pass to overrun Yan and Zhao, found no foe, and turned back.

literal: On day jiwei, Yuguli rebelled; Shilu was ordered to take troops and punish him.
idiomatic: On jiwei day Yuguli rose in revolt, and Shilu was sent with troops to suppress him.

literal: On day renwu in the fourth month of summer, he invested Youzhou but could not take it.
idiomatic: On renwu day in the fourth summer month he besieged Youzhou and failed to capture it.

literal: On day yisi in the sixth month, gazing at the city he saw vapor like smoke and fire; the Emperor said: "It is not yet time to attack.
idiomatic: On yisi day in the sixth month he looked at the city and saw a vapor like smoke and flame; the Emperor said, "We must not attack yet.

literal: " Because of great heat and torrential rains, the army withdrew.
idiomatic: " With the midsummer heat and ceaseless rain, he drew the army off.

literal: Helu and Lu Guoyong were left to hold it.
idiomatic: Helu and Lu Guoyong were left to garrison the place.

literal: Lige and his son Saibaoli rebelled and entered Youzhou.
idiomatic: Lige and his son Saibaoli defected and fled into Youzhou.

literal: In the eighth month of autumn, Li Cun sent Li Siyuan and others to relieve Youzhou; Helu and the rest withdrew for lack of numbers.
idiomatic: In the eighth autumn month Li Cun dispatched Li Siyuan and others to rescue Youzhou, and Helu and his fellows pulled back for want of men.

literal: On day bingshen in the first month of spring in the third year, his imperial brother Anduan was made Great Inner tiyin and ordered to attack Yun Prefecture and the southwestern tribes.
idiomatic: In the third year, on bingshen day of the first spring month, his brother Anduan was appointed Great Inner tiyin and charged to attack Yun Prefecture and the tribes of the southwest.

literal: In the second month, the Dadan state sent envoys on a friendly visit.
idiomatic: In the second month the Dadan kingdom sent envoys on a courtesy mission.

literal: On day guihai, the imperial capital was walled; Minister of Rites Kang Mojie was made commissioner of construction.
idiomatic: On guihai day they walled the imperial capital, and Kang Mojie, Minister of Rites, was put in charge of the work.

literal: Liang sent envoys on a friendly visit.
idiomatic: Liang sent envoys on a courtesy mission.

literal: Jin, Wuyue, Bohai, Goryeo, Uighur, Zubu, Xiang, and the prefectures of You, Zhen, Ding, Wei, Lu, and others each sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: Jin, Wuyue, Bohai, Goryeo, the Uighurs, the Zubu, the Xiang, and the prefectures of You, Zhen, Ding, Wei, Lu, and the rest all sent tribute envoys.

literal: On day yisi in the fourth month of summer, his imperial brother Dielege plotted rebellion; the affair was discovered; knowing guilt deserved death, he prepared a grave pit in advance, yet the kinsmen pleaded for pardon.
idiomatic: On yisi day in the fourth summer month his brother Dielege conspired to rebel; the plot came to light. Knowing he deserved death, he had a burial pit dug beforehand, but his clansmen begged for mercy.

literal: The Emperor had long hated the wife of his brother Yindishi, Nieligun, and therefore said: "If Nieligun can die in his stead, then I will consent.
idiomatic: The Emperor had always loathed his brother Yindishi's wife Nieligun, and said, "If Nieligun will die in his place, I will agree.

literal: " Nieligun hanged herself in the pit, and the slave Nügu and the rebel Heluzhi were buried alive there with her.
idiomatic: " Nieligun strangled herself in the pit, and the bondservant Nügu and the traitor Heluzhi were entombed alive beside her.

literal: Dielege was then pardoned.
idiomatic: Dielege was then forgiven.

literal: On day yihai in the fifth month, an edict ordered temples built to Confucius, to the Buddha, and to the Dao.
idiomatic: On yihai day in the fifth month he decreed the building of a Confucian temple, Buddhist monasteries, and Daoist abbeys.

literal: Collation Notes
idiomatic: Collation Notes

literal: 1: Xi Laiyi Shilie — Zhang Yuanji's collation notes
idiomatic: 1: Xi Laiyi Shilie — Zhang Yuanji's collation notes

literal: (hereinafter abbreviated as Zhang Collation)]〉
idiomatic: (hereinafter abbreviated as Zhang Collation)]〉

literal: Citing Officials' Register, vol. 1, "shilie means county," and Officials' Register, vol. 2, "milai means township," he argues that the character for township should not follow after shilie.
idiomatic: He cites Officials' Register, vol. 1 — "shilie is a county" — and vol. 2 — "milai is a township" — and holds that the township character should not be appended after shilie.

literal: According to the Explanation of the National Language, shilie is also a township, and milai is a smaller subdivision of township.
idiomatic: The Explanation of the National Language, however, also defines shilie as a township and milai as a smaller township unit.

literal: In "shilie township," the character for township is likewise redundant.
idiomatic: In "shilie township," the word township is redundant as well.

literal: Checking the text below, Taizu year seven, sixth month, Xialai County, and in Guards Record, lower section, Six Yuan Department, Xialan Shilie — all are variant renderings of this same name.
idiomatic: Below, in Taizu's seventh year, sixth month, Xialai County, and in the lower section of the Guards Record, Six Yuan Department, Xialan Shilie — each is a variant translation of the same name.

literal: The character for township is spurious.
idiomatic: The township character is a spurious addition.

literal: 2: "Campaign against Hedong and northern Dai" — northern Dai; the original text erroneously read "northern campaign," corrected according to Military Guards Record, upper section, and the Yongle Encyclopedia
idiomatic: 2: "Campaign against Hedong and northern Dai" — for northern Dai, the original erroneously read "northern campaign"; the correction follows Military Guards Record, upper section, and the Yongle Encyclopedia

idiomatic: (cited in the textual verification of the Daoguang Hall edition)]〉

idiomatic: 3: Ru'erwang Assembly Mound — the account of Taizong's tenth month in the fifth year reads Ru'erzheng Assembly Mound.

literal: 4: On the dingwei new moon in the fourth month of summer, Tang's Liang King Zhu Quanzhong deposed his sovereign and soon murdered him — Qian Daxin's Examination of Discrepancies in the Twenty-Two Histories
idiomatic: 4: On the dingwei new moon of the fourth summer month, Zhu Quanzhong, Liang King of Tang, deposed his lord and soon killed him — Qian Daxin's Examination of Discrepancies in the Twenty-Two Histories

idiomatic: (hereinafter abbreviated as Examination of Discrepancies)]〉

idiomatic: Citing Ouyang Xiu's Historical Records of the Five Dynasties

idiomatic: , the Liang ruler took the throne on jiazi day in the fourth month; in the first month of the next year he "murdered the King of Jiyin."

literal: To place it on the new moon of the fourth month is an error.
idiomatic: Placing the event on the fourth-month new moon is mistaken.

literal: 5: "Hedong Li Keyong died" — the character for "died," supplemented per Zhang Collation.
idiomatic: 5: "Hedong Li Keyong died" — the word died is supplied per Zhang Collation.

literal: 6: "The Empress urgently dispatched Shugulu to rescue it" — Shugulu; Ceremonial Guards Record, vol. 4, reads Hegulu, which is correct.
idiomatic: 6: "The Empress urgently sent Shugulu to the rescue" — for Shugulu, Ceremonial Guards Record, vol. 4, reads Hegulu, which is correct.

literal: 7: Inquiring of the younger brothers, facing Mount Muye, shooting ghost-arrows for exorcism — Feng Jiasheng's First Collation of the History of Liao
idiomatic: 7: "Inquiring of the younger brothers, facing Mount Muye, shooting ghost-arrows for exorcism" — Feng Jiasheng's First Collation of the History of Liao

idiomatic: states that inquire should read hear.

literal: 8: "Jin's military governor of Youzhou Lu Guoyong came to surrender" — this duplicates Lu Wenjin's surrender in the second month of the following year.
idiomatic: 8: "Jin military governor of Youzhou Lu Guoyong came to surrender" — this repeats Lu Wenjin's defection in the second month of the next year.

literal: Examination of Discrepancies further argues that at this time the military governor of Youzhou was Zhou Dewei, so he could not simultaneously be Lu Guoyong.
idiomatic: Examination of Discrepancies adds that Zhou Dewei was governor of Youzhou at the time, so Lu Guoyong cannot have held the same post.

literal: Because Wenjin was military governor of Ping Prefecture under the Khitan, the Khitan title he was granted was mistakenly taken for a Tang office.
idiomatic: Wenjin had been made Khitan governor of Ping Prefecture, and that Khitan appointment was wrongly recorded as a Tang office.

literal: Collated edition of Xue Juzheng's History of the Five Dynasties
idiomatic: Collated edition of Xue Juzheng's History of the Five Dynasties

idiomatic: (hereinafter abbreviated as Old History of the Five Dynasties)]〉

literal: Juan 97: Wenjin's courtesy name was Guoyong; New History of the Five Dynasties, juan 48, reads Dayong.
idiomatic: Juan 97: Wenjin's courtesy name was Guoyong; New History of the Five Dynasties, juan 48, gives Dayong.

literal: 9: Li Si'en's son Wuba — Si'en; the original text erroneously read "Siben."
idiomatic: 9: Li Si'en's son Wuba — for Si'en, the original erroneously read Siben.

literal: According to the biographies of Li Siben in the New and Old Histories of the Five Dynasties, neither mentions a son named Wuba.
idiomatic: The biographies of Li Siben in the New and Old Histories of the Five Dynasties nowhere mention a son Wuba.

literal: Checking Old History of the Five Dynasties, juan 52, Biography of Li Si'en: "He had two sons; the elder was called Wuba… he fought the Khitan at Xin Prefecture and died there.
idiomatic: Old History of the Five Dynasties, juan 52, Biography of Li Si'en, reads: "He had two sons; the elder was called Wuba… he fought the Khitan at Xin Prefecture and died there.
